A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProxyThinker with the same authors and core method. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization and changed experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original SFT/GRPO experiments on CV-Bench, ProxyThinker benchmark evaluations, hyperparameter and pass@k studies, and measured inference times.

after.justification: v2 retains original ProxyThinker evaluations and reports additional benchmark results, decoding ablations, reasoning-pattern classifications, expert-quality experiments, and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The three-model logit adjustment and shared autoregressive feedback procedure are unchanged: v1 Equation 1 becomes v2 Equation 2. The expanded implementation discussion clarifies existing vLLM scheduling. The new modified contrastive-decoding procedure is an experimental comparator, not a replacement for ProxyThinker.

E1.justification: v2 removes the SAT-15k training study and dedicated CV-Bench evaluation of counting, spatial relations, depth, and distance. It replaces the main quantitative MMMU evaluation with MMMU-Pro, including expanded-choice and vision-only settings, and adds EMMA's cross-modal reasoning problems. The original MMMU failure case remains in Appendix A.4.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated modified contrastive-decoding comparator, z_base + alpha*z_expert, in Figure 4 and VLAA-Thinker-3B in Table 5. It removes the CV-Bench comparison containing Qwen2-VL SFT and GRPO models, including Qwen2-VL-7B-SFT. Comparator membership in the retained main mathematical comparisons otherwise remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include GPT-4o-mini classification of reasoning patterns across 3,040 MathVision samples, a 32B base with 3B expert/amateur configuration, bfloat16 weight-memory profiling, and an average-gain summary metric. The 2B/7B spatial training and evaluation settings disappear. Retained experiments preserve greedy decoding, default alpha=0.5, and the original pass@k subset and sampling settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds an amateur-model ablation, quantitative reasoning-pattern analysis, R1-Bench subject breakdown, weak-expert negative-transfer study, and computational-overhead analysis. It removes the SFT-versus-GRPO spatial study and OpenVLThinker's hyperparameter sweep. The VL-Rethinker sweep, pass@k analysis, and existing qualitative success and failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same pass@k estimator and provide no confidence intervals, error bars, significance-test procedures, or experimental seed reporting. The new reasoning-pattern counts are descriptive results rather than a change in uncertainty estimation. References to statistical significance remain unsupported by a specified test in both versions.

E6.justification: v2 adds MMMU-Pro results, EMMA accuracy of 35.3% versus the 32B base's 31.1%, and the weak-expert configuration's MathVista score of 51.5% versus the base's 74.7%. CV-Bench and quantitative MMMU results are removed. Matched main-table entries also change: 32B/VL-Rethinker MathVerse rises from 55.1 to 55.3, and the 72B base's R1-Bench score changes from 52.0 to 50.4. However, v2 Section 4.1 and Table 5 still report 55.1.

T1.justification: v2 removes the background KL-regularized RFT objective and adds Appendix C's FLOP accounting and derivation of an approximately 93-billion-token break-even point under explicit utilization and per-token-cost assumptions. The decoding mathematics and pass@k estimator remain unchanged; no new correctness theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims of training-free reasoning transfer, competitive performance, and efficient inference remain. However, v2's introduction drops the specific claim of successful 2B-to-7B RFT transfer contrasted with unsuccessful SFT transfer. Broad claims about spatial improvements remain in the abstract and conclusion despite removal of the dedicated spatial experiment.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets the amateur model as essential for calibrating expert logits, argues for a domain-general reasoning prior, and explains negative transfer from weak or undersized experts. It also interprets quantitative backtracking, verification, and subgoal patterns and discusses cumulative inference costs and memory tradeoffs. The existing knowledge-intensive failure limitation remains, while Appendix D adds cross-tokenizer alignment as a possible mitigation.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies the existing vLLM implementation's KV caching, continuous batching, and separate scheduling variants. Appendix C documents DeepSpeed memory profiling, bfloat16 weights, and cited training hardware/time inputs used for resource estimates. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun. The code link, expert prompts, scoring prompts, and pass@k implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting MMMU-Pro, EMMA, VLAA-Thinker, cross-tokenizer mapping, and computational-resource analysis, while dropping SAT and Cambrian-1 references. Its positioning relative to DExperts, ProxyTuning, contrastive decoding, and visual model merging largely remains unchanged. DoLa's discussion is relocated rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: v2 consolidates preliminaries and method into a Methodology section, merges motivation with method exposition, revises selected introduction and implementation paragraphs, and moves DoLa into related work. It expands the appendix organization and adds an LLM-use disclosure. Most retained prose and the overall narrative remain recognizable rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document template and redraws Figure 1. Figure 3 distinguishes three implementation schedules, while Figure 4 changes from panels organized by expert to panels organized by benchmark with a new comparator. The CV-Bench table disappears; the main table changes benchmark and adds a gain column. New behavior, domain, expert-quality, and memory tables substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: The amateur-model ablation, systematic reasoning-pattern counts, and weak-expert experiment make the mechanism and failure boundaries more assessable than v1's largely qualitative treatment. Resource accounting also makes deployment tradeoffs clearer. These gains are partly offset by removing the SFT-versus-RFT spatial comparison and quantitative MMMU evidence while retaining broad spatial claims. Inconsistent MathVerse reporting also remains. Overall, the revision improves evidential depth, but the losses and reporting weaknesses limit the net improvement.
